q: What do we know about feat-cb-handoff-rule-v2 in the chatbot-deflection project?
a: feat-cb-handoff-rule-v2 hands a chat to an agent after three failed intent matches (v1 used two). On the 14-day repeat window it gives 15 percent repeat contact against 21 percent for v1, at 25 percent containment against 29 percent (exp-304, Jan to Mar 2026, n = 96,000 sessions).

q: What came of exp-302 in chatbot-deflection?
a: exp-302 (25 percent randomised A/B, closed 2026-03-16, n = 142,000 sessions) cut calls per 1,000 eligible sessions by only 6.1 percent, far below what 34 percent containment implies. That produced fnd-cb-volume-shift, which fed dec-cb-rollout-60 on 2026-06-15.

q: What does cb-intent-v2 in the chatbot-deflection project use?
a: cb-intent-v2 uses the 384-dim message embedding from feat-cb-intent-embed-v1 and the account-state features from feat-cb-account-state-v1. It is trained on the labelled messages in ds-cb-intent-eval and replaced cb-intent-v1 on 2026-03-26.

q: What is the current handoff rule in the chatbot-deflection project?
a: feat-cb-handoff-rule-v2: hand off after three failed intent matches, with the count resetting after a successful answer. It supersedes feat-cb-handoff-rule-v1 (two failures) and was adopted in dec-cb-handoff-v2 on 2026-05-06.

q: What AUC does the escalation model cb-escalate-v1 reach in the chatbot-deflection project, and on which set?
a: AUC 0.77 on the holdout-2025q4 escalation sessions (n = 18,400, Oct to Dec 2025), measured in exp-305 on 2026-02-12.

q: Why did the chatbot-deflection project move its containment window to 48 hours?
a: A 24-hour call window overstated containment: the same v1 replay gave 34 percent with 24 hours and 29 percent with 48 hours (exp-306). That sensitivity, with the 21 percent 14-day repeat contact in fnd-cb-repeat-contact, led to dec-cb-metric-48h on 2026-05-04, which superseded dec-cb-metric-24h.
